articles.title: Cardinals hopeful RB Jeremiyah Love can play vs. Chargers in Week 1 after preseason ankle injury
articles.summary: Jeremiyah Love, who the Cardinals took with the No. 3 overall pick in the draft, went down with an ankle sprain earlier in the preseason and has been sidelin...
articles.body:
A decision hasn't been made just yet, but the Arizona Cardinals are hopeful that new running back Jeremiyah Love will be able to take the field on Sunday afternoon in Los Angeles.

Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Monday he's optimistic that Love, who went down with a high ankle sprain earlier in the preseason , will be able to play in their season opener against the Chargers. Love was "moving around" during the team's walkthrough on Monday and is progressing, though the team won't issue their first injury report until Wednesday.

"I feel good [about his chances]," LaFleur said, via ESPN .

Love went down with an ankle sprain during their preseason win over the Las Vegas Raiders after he made a catch near the goal line and was brought down to the field awkwardly. Love ended up playing 23 snaps in that game, and had 58 rushing yards on 11 carries before he was injured.

The Cardinals selected Love with the No. 3 overall pick in the draft earlier this year out of Notre Dame. He had 1,372 rushing yards and 21 total touchdowns in his final season with the Fighting Irish, and he finished in third in the Heisman Trophy race.

The Cardinals went 3-14 last season. They kept three running backs on their 53-man roster, including Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight. They'll open the 2026 campaign against the Chargers at SoFi Stadium on Sunday afternoon (4:25 p.m. ET, CBS).

While it's unclear if Love will be able to make his NFL debut as scheduled, it doesn't sound like a return is far off.

articles.title: Titans LB Cedric Gray in concussion protocol ahead of season opener after UTV crash
articles.summary: Cedric Gray suffered a concussion and other minor injuries while driving a UTV over the holiday weekend.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans may be without standout linebacker Cedric Gray for the start of the season after he was involved in a UTV accident over the weekend.

The Titans revealed on Monday that Gray had been placed in the NFL's concussion protocol after a utility terrain vehicle crash. Gray was the driver of the UTV and sustained "minor injuries" and a concussion, though specifics of the crash are not yet known. A team source told ESPN's Turron Davenport that there was no alcohol or reckless driving involved.

"We look forward to Cedric returning to the field soon and in full health when he clears the NFL's concussion protocol," the team said, in part.

The Titans selected Gray in the fourth round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of North Carolina. The 23-year-old led the team with 164 total tackles last season, his first as a starter.

Gray could still be cleared in time to play in the Titans' season opener on Sunday if he gets through the concussion protocol in time. But his status for that game, considering the timing of the accident, is in doubt.

The Titans went 3-14 in 2025 and missed the playoffs for a second straight season. They've since hired Robert Saleh as their head coach. The Titans will host the New York Jets (1 p.m. ET, CBS), the last team that Saleh served as the head coach for, on Sunday afternoon at Nissan Stadium.

articles.body: The John Harbaugh era meant change for the New York Giants, but as Week 1 officially got started on Monday, a surprising one came to the 53-man roster. Wide receiver Darius Slayton, the longest-tenured Giants player entering the 2026 NFL season, was surprisingly released despite initially making the roster out of training camp, the team announced. JOHN HARBAUGH AND JAXSON DART AIM TO PULL THE NEW YORK GIANTS OUT OF THE NFC EAST BASEMENT Slayton was a fifth-round draft pick out of Auburn in 2019, where he showed much promise after going for 740 yards on 48 receptions with eight touchdowns. articles.title: Tom Brady Talks Broadcasting Future amid Massive Fox Contract, Raiders Ownership
articles.summary: Tom Brady has built quite the business portfolio following his NFL retirement, but he has no plans to put his broadcast career on the back burner.
articles.body:
Tom Brady has built quite the business portfolio following his NFL retirement, but he has no plans to put his broadcast career on the back burner.

Fox Sports president Brad Zager said that Brady is in the broadcasting game "for the long haul."

"From the moment we signed Tom, no matter what was written or said, I have never gotten an indication from Tom that he is not into this for the long haul," Zager said, per Richard Deitsch and Austin Karp of Sports Business Journal. "For over a decade, we also heard about [Aikman] possibly taking a front office job. Rumors like that were always out there. You don't know what the future holds, but I can tell you right now that we have had no discussions with Tom that didn't involve him being here for a long time."

Will a non-QB be 2027's No. 1 pick? New NFL mock draft

Brady signed a massive 10-year, $375 million deal with Fox, and he has every intention of fulfilling it.

"I have a lot to prove to myself, to my teammates. I have a lot to prove to the executives," Brady said. "I want to go earn it and I don't want anything given to me. I hope they'll have me through the end of this contract. I love getting to enjoy the game. I love watching good football. There's such great camaraderie and chemistry we all have together. We have seminars. We have off-site retreats. We have text threads with all of us. It feels like a big family in so many ways, and I was not really expecting that when I decided to take the job."

Brady has a few limitations on what kind of access he gets to players and coaches due to his standing as a minority owner of the Las Vegas Raiders, but he said that doesn't impact his ability to prepare for each game he calls.

"It's clickbait for people and it's something that people have no idea what they're really glomming onto," Brady said. "They just put it out there in the world and see what sticks. So to me, I just focus on what I need to do to be prepared. That's what I did as a player, and I go out there every week as a broadcaster and try to do the same thing."

Brady is entering his third season as an analyst with Fox, and he'll make his season debut on Sunday when the Philadelphia Eagles host the Washington Commanders at 4:25 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Could Dianna Russini return to NFL coverage? Mike Florio hints at a possible comeback before the Patriots opener

Front Office Sports reported that Russini is “absolutely” planning to return to sports media. The report said she has considered different roles, including another NFL insider position and a more personality-focused role.That could make her next move particularly interesting. Russini spent years building a reputation as a well-connected NFL reporter, first at ESPN and later as The Athletic's lead NFL insider. A return would give her another chance to rebuild her career after one of the most closely watched media controversies of the offseason.What did The Athletic find about Mike Vrabel and Dianna Russini?The Athletic's internal review added important context to the story. Editorial director Mike Semel wrote that Russini's relationship with Vrabel “was in clear violation of The Athletic's standards.” He said the relationship should have been disclosed, regardless of its nature.However, the investigation did not find a clear link between the relationship and Russini's reporting. The review examined 903 articles, 77 videos and more than 200 podcast episodes connected to her work. Only a small portion focused on Vrabel, the Patriots or his former team, the Tennessee Titans.Semel also acknowledged that some of Russini's coverage of Vrabel looked “awkward or even uncomfortable” in hindsight. That distinction matters because The Athletic found a standards violation without establishing that Russini deliberately promoted Vrabel through her journalism.Meanwhile, Vrabel has moved his attention back to the Patriots. He addressed the investigation during a Patriots press conference and made it clear that he wanted to move forward with the upcoming season.Now, Florio's latest report has shifted attention back to Russini. If his prediction proves accurate, her return could put one of the NFL's biggest media stories right back in the conversation just as the Patriots begin their season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “I am trying to do that as much as possible”: How Patrick Mahomes’ growing business empire is now turning his off-field dream into reality
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes had already conquered much of the NFL world when he started thinking about life beyond football. In April 2021, the Kansas City Chiefs.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes had already conquered much of the NFL world when he started thinking about life beyond football. In April 2021, the Kansas City Chiefs star openly said he wanted to build an empire away from the field.Now, that ambition has taken shape through sports ownership, production and investments in performance technology. Mahomes is no longer simply using his fame to promote brands. He is putting his money behind businesses and teams he believes can grow. How did Patrick Mahomes turn his off-field ambition into a growing business empire?Patrick Mahomes explained his plans during a Yahoo Finance Presents interview in 2021. He was just 25 at the time, but his business ambitions had already moved well beyond traditional endorsement deals. After signing his record-setting 10-year, $503 million Chiefs contract in 2020, Mahomes bought a minority stake in the Kansas City Royals and invested an undisclosed amount in Whoop, which was then valued at about $1.2 billion.“I am trying to build an empire off the field in every way,” Mahomes said during that interview. He then explained how athletes such as Michael Jordan and Alex Rodriguez influenced his thinking, adding, “I watch a lot of the great athletes that came before me and they found ways to build their empire and to build themselves up off the field, so I am trying to do that as much as possible.”His actions since then have followed that idea. Mahomes joined the ownership group of the Kansas City Current in 2022 alongside his wife, Brittany Mahomes. The Current's official profile also identifies him as a co-owner of the Kansas City Royals and Sporting Kansas City, while listing him as the founder of 2PM Productions. His involvement with the Current also made him the first active NFL player to hold equity in an NWSL team.Then came Formula 1. In October 2023, Mahomes joined an investment group that took a stake in Alpine F1. He explained at the time that he had been watching the sport grow and wanted to take advantage of the opportunity. Mahomes also made it clear that his interest in sports ownership had not stopped there, saying he was always looking around for opportunities outside the NFL.That pattern says more about his strategy than any single investment. Mahomes has gradually moved from being the face of brands to becoming an owner and investor himself. His portfolio now touches baseball, women's soccer, MLS, Formula 1, entertainment and sports technology, giving him interests that extend far beyond his work as the Chiefs quarterback. Why does Patrick Mahomes’ investment strategy make his 2021 business dream look more real today?Whoop remains one of the clearest examples of the strategy working. Patrick Mahomes invested in the wearable technology company when it carried a valuation of roughly $1.2 billion. On March 31, 2026, Whoop announced a $575 million Series G funding round at a $10.1 billion valuation. That is a major jump from the company's valuation when Mahomes first invested. However, his investment amount and exact ownership stake remain private, so his personal return cannot be calculated from the valuation alone.The bigger story, though, is not just Whoop. Mahomes has repeatedly chosen businesses and sports properties that connect with his interests. His investment in Alpine gave him a place inside one of the world's fastest-growing sports properties, while his ownership positions in Kansas City teams keep him closely connected to the city where his NFL career took off. His role with 2PM Productions also shows that he is building something on the media side rather than relying entirely on football income.Mahomes has also been open about the fact that investing does not always work out. During the same 2021 Yahoo Finance interview, he admitted that some of his investments had not been successful. Instead of treating those setbacks as a reason to stop, he explained the lesson he took from them.“The biggest thing is to do the stuff you love and you have a passion for because if you do that, you usually figure out a way to make it work,” Mahomes said. He added that he wanted to invest in things he “truly believe[d] in.”In 2021, Mahomes talked about following athletes who built lasting empires beyond their playing careers. And currently, he has ownership across multiple sports, a production company and early investments that have grown alongside major businesses. The exact value of his private portfolio remains unknown, but the direction is obvious. Mahomes did not just talk about building something beyond the Chiefs. He has spent the years since that interview putting the pieces together.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Aaron Donald Gives Update on Week 1 Status vs. 49ers amid Return from Retirement
articles.summary: The NFL world is waiting to see whether Aaron Donald will play in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, but the Los Angeles Rams star defensive tackle — fresh off his return from retirement — isn't ready to give an answer yet.
articles.body:
The NFL world is waiting to see whether Aaron Donald will play in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, but the Los Angeles Rams star defensive tackle — fresh off his return from retirement — isn't ready to give an answer yet.

The Rams are set to travel to Melbourne for the season opener on Tuesday night, and Donald wouldn't commit to saying whether he'll be on the flight.

"Taking it day by day. Come up with a game plan to see what's going on," Donald told reporters Monday. "Feeling good, feeling really good. Come up with a game plan and see.

Will a non-QB be 2027's No. 1 pick? New NFL mock draft

"Honestly, man, I really do feel good. Things are clicking faster than I thought it would be. Even my first day out there, with 11-on-11, things would be a little all over the place. Settled in. A couple of plays a little rusty. It ain't where I want it to be, but it's pretty damn good if you ask me. To not play football in two years, to be moving how I'm moving, it's really no dropoff. It's not where I want to be. I can see it. I know there are things I want to clean up, that I'm going to clean up. The more reps I do, the more I play, it'll get there."

Donald hasn't played in an NFL game since 2023, and he didn't officially sign with the Rams until two weeks ago. A quick ramp-up time would make playing a game in a different time zone after a lengthy flight quite difficult.

Donald has been getting into NFL shape since June, so he wouldn't be going into the game completely out of shape. Still, he's no spring chicken.

The Rams, of course, want Donald on the field as soon as possible, but they have plenty of talent on the defensive line, so there's not exactly a huge rush to have him.

Whether the three-time Defensive Player of the Year will begin his season in Week 1 should become clearer by Tuesday evening.

articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes survived a torn ACL only to face a brand new threat from inside his own offensive line
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes is back. Nine months after tearing his ACL against the Chargers, he is set to start for the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1 against the D.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is back. Nine months after tearing his ACL against the Chargers, he is set to start for the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1 against the Denver Broncos. For most quarterbacks, surviving that injury and returning in under a year would be the story. For Mahomes, it is only the beginning of a much messier situation. Because the bigger concern right now is not what happened to him last December. It is what could happen to him this September, courtesy of the man assigned to protect his blindside.Is Josh Simmons' blocking technique putting Patrick Mahomes at risk?The short answer is yes, and it is not just fan speculation. Danny Heifetz of The Ringer Fantasy Football Show put it bluntly on September 7. "I think Patrick Mahomes is gonna tear his ACL again," Heifetz said on the podcast. His reasoning had two layers. The first is that nine months is about the fastest any quarterback has returned from an ACL tear with any real success, raising questions about whether Mahomes is truly ready or simply determined to be.The second layer is more specific and more troubling. Left tackle Josh Simmons uses a blocking move known as the snatch technique, where he grabs a pass rusher by the shoulder pads and whips him down and to the left. Under normal circumstances, it is an aggressive, effective move. But with Mahomes standing in the pocket behind him, that defender gets thrown directly into the quarterback's legs."Gonna [throw] him into [Mahomes'] legs," co-host Danny Kelly noted during the same podcast discussion.What makes this more than just broadcast commentary is who else is raising the alarm. Mitchell Schwartz, the former Chiefs right tackle who was arguably their best offensive lineman during their first Super Bowl run, has repeatedly flagged the issue on social media. Heifetz confirmed this on air, saying Schwartz "just keeps posting on Twitter that Josh Simmons should not be using that technique because eventually Patrick Mahomes will be there, and he's gonna be in the pocket more this season because of the [lack of] mobility."That last part is critical. Mahomes coming off an ACL tear is not the same Mahomes who could scramble out of danger on instinct. He will take longer to process, longer to move, and will stay in the pocket far more than usual. Which means any defender landing near his legs is not a near-miss. It is a direct threat.Does the Chiefs' offense have enough around Mahomes to carry this season?Simmons' blocking habits are one problem. His availability is another. The 2025 first-round pick missed nine games during his rookie season and is now dealing with a back injury that kept him out of practice and could sideline him for the Week 1 opener against Denver entirely. If that happens, an undrafted rookie free agent steps in to guard the most important player on the field.Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer raised the broader offensive concern on Monday, questioning whether Kansas City invested enough this offseason to actually support Mahomes. The Chiefs poured resources into defense while banking on two high-risk, high-reward draft picks to carry the offense."What could determine it largely rests on two guys the Chiefs took risks on in the draft," Breer wrote. "They have very high ceilings and, as we've seen, very low floors: left tackle Josh Simmons and receiver Rashee Rice. If those guys are playing to their potential, Kansas City could have another Super Bowl team on its hands. If they're unavailable or in disrepair for large chunks of the season, the likelihood of that is lessened."Rice brings his own injury history. Simmons brings a back problem and a blocking tendency that worries former offensive linemen who know exactly what those moves do to a quarterback's knees. And Mahomes, for all his greatness, is walking into Sunday carrying a rebuilt knee and reduced mobility.The Chiefs did not just need their left tackle healthy. They needed him smart. Right now, they might not have either.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why Justin Herbert's 2026 season could be the most dangerous in Chargers history
articles.summary: NFL News: Justin Herbert has had good seasons. But 2026 is shaping up to be something different. With Mike McDaniel calling plays as offensive coordinator and a.
articles.body: Justin Herbert has had good seasons. But 2026 is shaping up to be something different. With Mike McDaniel calling plays as offensive coordinator and a deeper receiving corps around him, analysts are already predicting Herbert could cross 5,000 passing yards for only the second time in his career. If that happens, he joins Drew Brees, Tom Brady, and Patrick Mahomes as the only quarterbacks in NFL history to do it more than once. That's not a conversation anyone was expecting to have about the Chargers this soon.Can Justin Herbert really throw for 5,000 yards again in 2026?Herbert did it once, back in 2021, when he threw for 5,014 yards and 38 touchdowns. It was one of the best statistical seasons any Chargers quarterback has ever had. And yet, Los Angeles finished 9-8 and missed the playoffs entirely. The numbers were there. The wins weren't.That tension is exactly what makes 2026 so fascinating. Keegan Abdoo of NFL.com's Next Gen Stats put it plainly in his bold prediction for the season: "Herbert joins Drew Brees (five), Tom Brady (two) and Patrick Mahomes (two) as the only quarterbacks in NFL history to throw for over 5,000 yards in multiple seasons. Herbert's elite arm strength recalibrates the precise timing of Mike McDaniel's play designs, elevating the offense to an even more explosive attack than McDaniel ever had in Miami."That last part deserves some weight. McDaniel built one of the most creative passing offenses in the league with Tua Tagovailoa in Miami. Herbert is a different kind of thrower. Bigger arm, more velocity, and a frame that gives him sight lines most quarterbacks don't have. McDaniel's timing-based system, combined with Herbert's natural gifts, could produce something genuinely difficult for defenses to solve.Herbert came close to 5,000 again in 2022, finishing with 4,739 yards. That season confirmed it wasn't a one-year aberration. The production is real. The question has always been whether the team around him could match what he's capable of.Will 5,000 passing yards actually help the Chargers win games this season?Here's where it gets complicated. A 5,000-yard passing season usually means the offense leaned heavily on the quarterback, often because the run game wasn't pulling its weight. For the Chargers to be a genuine playoff team in 2026, they need balance, not just numbers.Running back Omarion Hampton enters his second NFL season with real expectations on his shoulders. After flashing potential as a rookie, Hampton is projected for a breakout year. If he delivers, it actually reduces pressure on Herbert to carry the offense alone. Fewer empty possessions, more manageable third downs, and a defense that doesn't spend extra time on the field.That's the paradox sitting at the center of this prediction. Herbert throwing for 5,000 yards might mean the Chargers are firing on all cylinders. Or it might mean Hampton underperformed and Los Angeles leaned too heavily on the pass again. The stat itself tells you the output, not the story behind it.What's clear is that Herbert, at this stage of his career, has the tools, the coordinator, and the roster depth to make 2026 his most complete season yet.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: AFC South 2026 Predictions: Can the Texans Run Away With the Division?
articles.summary: The AFC South is usually one of the more hectic divisions in football, making it nearly impossible to predict who will win. That trend should continue in 202...
articles.body:
The AFC South is usually one of the more hectic divisions in football, making it nearly impossible to predict who will win. That trend should continue in 2026, with all of these teams looking to take the crown, each with a legitimate reason.

Looking at it on paper, there's a clear frontrunner, though, who should be one of the best teams in the entire AFC. Here are my predictions for the AFC South in 2026.

Houston, we have a problem. This defense is about to terrorize the NFL. The Houston Texans defense was one of the best last season and proved it in the playoffs against New England. The issue was the offense, but the scary part is this defense got even better. One aspect that could've improved from last season was the interior of the defensive line, and Houston addressed that by drafting Kayden McDonald in the second round. 6-foot-3 and 326 pounds of pure run-stuffing power is what McDonald brings to this defense.

Outside of interior rushing defense, edge rush and secondary depth were two other areas Houston addressed. Well, general manager Nick Caserio is on top of it by signing Jadeveon Clowney and drafting Kamari Ramsey . This unit, led by Matt Burke, will be lights-out and a big reason the Texans have a high floor.

Now, the offense. It's been the talking point all offseason long, due to CJ Stroud's performance in the playoffs. If this unit can be a top-15 offense, Houston should run away with this division. Stroud gets a ton of blame thrown at him, but the rushing game was horrendous last season. No other way to put it. This offseason, Houston made sure to raise the floor of its rushing game by adding David Montgomery , Keylan Rutledge , Wyatt Teller, and Braden Smith . Those additions should help plenty. Expect this Texans team to get off to a hot start and take the NFL by storm.

It doesn't make up for it, but I do feel low on the Indianapolis Colts and could see them playing even better than this. The injury to Daniel Jones is concerning, but from everything coming out of training camp, he looks healthy. Despite the losses of Michael Pittman Jr. , Kwity Paye , and Nick Cross , this is a Colts roster still loaded with talent.

The team clearly trusts receiver Alec Pierce after giving him a four-year, $114 million contract this offseason. He and Josh Downs will enter Year 2 with Jones, so expect them to look even better. Not to mention, Shane Steichen is one of the best play-callers in the NFL. He still has his main weapons in Jonathan Taylor and Tyler Warren ; this is an underrated offense that can steal some tough games throughout the schedule.

Looking at the defense, the main holes were the linebacker corps. General manager Chris Ballard signed Akeem Davis-Gather and drafted CJ Allen in the 2026 NFL Draft. The starting 11 on the defensive end can be one of the best units in the NFL, but the depth behind it is lacking. The edge room had some standouts in the preseason, but how much can the Colts really rely on Caden Curry and Michael Clemons if they had to play starting reps? That's the one aspect of this team that worries me, which is a big part of why I don't see them winning double-digit games in 2026.

It just hurts to have the Jacksonville Jaguars under .500 next year, 'cause I like this team. The Jaguars' offense was one of the best units in the back half of the 2025 season, and I expect that to continue in 2026. Head coach Liam Coen and defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile both excel at their roles. Each has the talent on both sides of the ball to have top-10 units, so why are the Jaguars under .500?

Well, when it came down to it, and it was time to pick games, it became hard to give them wins. Road games in Denver, Cincinnati, Baltimore, Chicago, Houston, and Dallas. As much as I like this Jaguars team, it's hard for me to give them wins against a lot of these other teams. Not to mention they host teams like New England, Philadelphia, and Pittsburgh.

It's just the reality sometimes within the NFL and predictions. The roster is there despite the questionable draft class, but I just don't see the Jaguars having the same success as last season. This prediction could look silly in a couple of months when Trevor Lawrence is playing lights out, and I'll just have to accept it then.

The Tennessee Titans have gotten way too much hype this offseason. Yes, the hiring of Robert Saleh and Brian Daboll was excellent. But truly look at this roster and ask yourself if they're ready to be a contender, even in their own division. The receiving core got major upgrades with Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson , which raises the floor of this offense, especially under Daboll. The one issue is the offensive line: I'm not fully sold on left tackle Dan Moore Jr. being consistently good, and the interior line, other than Peter Skoronski .

Defensively, much of it will fall on Saleh's shoulders to get this unit operating at an elite level. Edge rusher is still a big question, and the question is who will step up. There are a lot of names in the room, such as Jacob Martin , Jermaine Johnson II , Keldric Faulk, and Femi Oladejo . Who's going to be that guy on third down? That question still needs to be answered. The secondary as well just doesn't seem to have a high ceiling. The players are good enough to operate within this Saleh team, but is it playoff caliber? No, it's not.

Tennessee is moving in the right direction, and Cam Ward should take a jump in his second year with Daboll. But they still have work to do, and having games against the AFC South, Dallas, Baltimore, and Philadelphia doesn't help.
